title: Workflow: Architecture Roguelike RPG Character Sprite Style Study
author: PigeonHeadArc
selftext:
Hey guys, 

I'm far enough in my game that I'm happy with the concept so today I started the process of actually caring about the visuals. It went pretty well using Claude for prompts (and tweaking) and CGPT for creating the images. I was able to get close to 90% of where I wanted my sprites to be. I could not figure out how to get the last 10%. 

**Claude suggest I try the following workflow (this following explanation is an AI generated copy paste of my new workflow):**

Stop *describing* the style every generation and just *train* it once. The recommended setup was:

* **ComfyUI** (node-based local image gen) — free
* **Flux.1** as the base model
* **Train a LoRA** on my own good renders so the style is baked in instead of prompted
* **ControlNet** to lock pose/proportions (my characters all need the same scale + facing direction)

The idea: the blank-face alien species + flat posterized look becomes part of the model, so I stop fighting it, and ControlNet handles the "always same body, always facing left" stuff.

**What you actually need + file sizes (rough)**

* **ComfyUI** – free, open source
* **Flux dev checkpoint** – \~23GB for the full fp16, or \~11GB if you grab the fp8 version (fp8 runs way lighter, barely a quality hit for this)
* **Flux text encoders** – t5xxl (\~5GB fp8 / \~9GB fp16) + clip\_l (\~250MB)
* **Flux VAE** – \~330MB
* **A ControlNet model for Flux** – anywhere from \~1.5GB to \~6GB depending which one
* **Your trained LoRA (the output)** – tiny, like 20–150MB depending on settings
* **Training images** – I'm using \~20-30 of my best ChatGPT renders

Realistically you want a decent GPU. Flux is happy around 12GB+ VRAM; you can squeeze it onto 8GB with the fp8/GGUF versions. Training a LoRA locally wants more headroom (\~16-24GB is comfy), but you can also train it in the cloud cheap if your card can't.

**Cost**

Running it all locally = **free** (just the disk space + your electricity). If you don't have the GPU for training, cloud LoRA trainers run like **$2-3 a training run**, so still basically nothing.

  
**Back to me, the human:** 

I tried it out. First time me doing anything like this locally. I was impressed, but the quality was crap compared to ChatGPT. I almost immediately pulled the plug but decided to add 5 more images to train LoRA. Output went from like 20% to about 60% and even gave me some really good idea (which GPT didn't). Unfortunately I got locked out of GPT till 8PM so I can't keep training my local AI. I'll experiment some more tonight and tomorrow and if I make any breakthroughs I'll repost my updated workflow. 

  
TLDR: CGPT is 90% successful at generating the style I want. Switched to local AI (first time) to train my own model (see workflow above). Current state is much worse than GPT but looks very promising. We'll report back soon.
